overview.title: Words in UI and reports: no decorative dashes, hype, filler, noise labels or padding; numbers over adjectives

language.check.effect: Run the no-slop CL-Skill checks on files or text; return each hit with file, line, match and fix
language.check.pre: Paths inside the workspace (or absolute) to Markdown, text, HTML or JSX; or inline text

check-file.goal: A report or UI file passes every block check of the no-slop skill

check-text.goal: A summary, label or message passes every block check before it is sent

cut.constraints: Removal test: if cutting the sentence loses no fact, number, step or decision, cut it. Openers that restate the task and closers that restate the body or offer help are cuts.
cut.question: Does each flagged sentence carry a fact, a number, a step or a decision the reader needs?

number.constraints: give = write the measured number with its unit next to the claim (37 ms, 4 of 6, $0.02); drop = delete the size word. Never invent a number.
number.question: For each size or speed word: is the measured number known?

pitfalls.failure: An em dash, en dash or spaced hyphen joins two thoughts or decorates a heading
pitfalls.recovery: Full stop for two thoughts, colon for a result or list, brackets for an aside; a tight en dash stays only in number or day ranges

pitfalls.failure: Hype or filler words (seamless, powerful, in order to, it's worth noting, breathing room) stand where a fact belongs
pitfalls.recovery: Delete the phrase; name the effect and its size

pitfalls.failure: A UI label is chatty or soothing (Your plan eyebrow, comfortably, just, simply, let's)
pitfalls.recovery: A label is the noun, the verb or the state: Plan limits, Slow down, 62% used

pitfalls.failure: A report opens with Here is or closes with Let me know / In summary
pitfalls.recovery: Start with the answer; stop when it is said

pitfalls.failure: much faster, a lot cheaper, several, significantly with no number in the sentence
pitfalls.recovery: Give the measured number or delete the word

pitfalls.failure: done() is refused with X language lines
pitfalls.recovery: Rewrite exactly the quoted lines, run language.check(path=...) on the file, then done() again

frontier: Tone that is clean by these checks but cold or rude needs a reader; word lists are English, dash and number rules apply to every language.
The host gate checks prose and UI files written during the task (.md .txt .html .jsx .tsx) and the done() summary; code comments and quoted sources are not checked.
guidance: Plain short sentences, 30 words or fewer; UI lines 14 words or fewer.
No em dash or en dash as punctuation, in headings too: 'Weekend plan: final note', not 'Weekend plan — final note'.
No hype (seamless, powerful, cutting-edge, leverage, unlock, elevate, delve, robust as praise) and no filler (in order to, it's worth noting, basically, essentially, at the end of the day).
UI labels name the thing, the action or the state; no eyebrow that repeats the title, no soothing words (comfortably, gently, breathing room, all set, just, simply).
Numbers over adjectives: 7x cheaper ($0.15 to $0.02), not much cheaper; 4 of 6 tests, not most tests. With no number, drop the adjective.
One hedge per sentence at most; say what is known and what is not.
Reports start with the result and stop when it is said: no 'Here is', 'Let me know', 'In summary', 'I hope this helps'.
Before done(), run language.check on every report and UI file you wrote; the host refuses done() while a block check fails and names each line.
The full rule set with sources is the CL-Skill manuals/skills/no-slop.cl; its checks are the same code the host runs.
